clue.text: Like some terraced houses, one after the other

blocks.note: first meaning: built in rows sharing a rear wall with the houses behind
second meaning: consecutively, in immediate succession

explanation.surface: A description of a street of terraced houses lined up one after another.
explanation.walkthrough: Back-to-back houses, common in northern English industrial towns, share their back wall with another row; the phrase also means in unbroken sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyphenated phrase is both an adjective for houses joined at the rear and an adverbial idiom for consecutive events.

clue.text: A piece pocketed by beautiful woman in game

indicators.note: something pocketed is tucked inside, so the woman's word holds the first pieces

blocks.note: taken as written
a gat is slang for a gun, also called a piece
a belle is a beautiful woman

explanation.surface: A gaming piece potted by a beautiful woman during a table game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece' and 'pocketed' suggest balls dropping into pockets, apt for the answer, but 'piece' is gangster slang for a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagatelle is a table game in which balls are struck into numbered holes, a forerunner of pinball.

clue.text: Work out with expert

blocks.note: first meaning: to solve
second meaning: first-rate

explanation.surface: Doing exercise alongside a professional trainer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work out' suggests the gym, but it means to solve.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb meaning to solve a puzzle and an adjective meaning highly skilled, as in crack troops.

clue.text: The enemy infiltrating the organisation in novel

indicators.note: an infiltrator gets inside a body, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: time is often called 'the enemy', as in 'time is the enemy'
THE plus MACHINE, an organised system such as a party machine

explanation.surface: Hostile agents penetrating a group, as in a spy story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The enemy' is an old byword for time, as in 'time, the enemy'; it slips into the middle of the organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Time Machine is the 1895 science-fiction novel by H. G. Wells.

clue.text: Fight about pot causes exhaustion

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the fight wraps round the pot

blocks.note: a bout is a boxing match or fight
an urn is a vase or pot

explanation.surface: A row over cannabis leaves everyone worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pot' tempts as cannabis, but it is a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Burnout is physical or mental collapse from overwork, a form of exhaustion.

clue.text: Girl with accountant going round a plant

indicators.note: going round means circling, so the accountant encloses what follows

blocks.note: CA is chartered accountant
taken as written
a mill is an industrial plant or factory

explanation.surface: A girl and her accountant walking around a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks botanical but is a factory. C...A wraps A MILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Camilla is a female given name, so it fits the crossword convention of girl for any woman's name.

clue.text: What the burglar took was awfully good

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so the preceding word's letters come out in a wrong order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
G is the standard abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A comment that a burglar's haul was rather impressive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully good' reads as one phrase meaning very good, but 'awfully' works on the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Swag is slang for stolen goods, the loot a burglar carries off.

clue.text: Now I began swimming in Wisconsin lake

indicators.note: swimming suggests moving about freely, so the letters drift into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: Someone taking a dip in an American lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface fits a lake so well that 'swimming' passes for scenery.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Winnebago is the largest inland lake in the US state of Wisconsin.

clue.text: Unfairly influenced foolish person to accept tons

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the foolish person holds the next piece

blocks.note: a goat is a fool, as in 'acting the goat'
T is the abbreviation for tons

explanation.surface: A gullible fool bribed with huge sums.
explanation.walkthrough: Goat for a fool is mainly British, as in 'stop acting the goat'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be got at is to be bribed or improperly pressured, so the phrase means unfairly influenced.

clue.text: Ordered as nightcap, beer might give one an opportunity to relax

indicators.note: ordered means put in a fresh arrangement, so the letters are re-sorted

blocks.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: A beer requested as a bedtime drink helps one unwind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' reads as asking for a drink at a bar, not as rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: A breathing space is a short pause or respite, giving time to rest or reflect.

clue.text: Famous cricketer, first to get run

indicators.note: first to points at only the opening letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: opening letter of get
a run or race is a contest of speed

explanation.surface: A celebrated cricketer being the first to score a run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run' looks like a cricket run but simply means a race. W. G. Grace was the great Victorian English cricketer.
explanation.definitionFit: W. G. Grace is a legendary figure in the history of English cricket, so he is an example of a famous player.

clue.text: Odd term to describe identifying mark of artist

indicators.note: odd here means strange or irregular, so the following word is rearranged
to describe in geometry is to draw a line around something, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged and split around the next piece
a brand is a mark that identifies an owner or maker

explanation.surface: Asking about a strange word for the signature that identifies a painter's work.
explanation.walkthrough: The scrambled word splits in two, three letters before the mark and one after.
explanation.definitionFit: Rembrandt van Rijn was a Dutch master painter, so the answer is an example of an artist.

clue.text: To accept or refuse the offer could be the thief's dilemma

definitions.text: To accept or refuse the offer

blocks.clueFragment: To accept or refuse the offer
blocks.note: first meaning: the phrase used when an offer is final and non-negotiable
second meaning, read literally: whether to steal an item or leave it where it is

explanation.surface: A take-or-refuse ultimatum compared to a thief weighing up whether to pocket something.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads the stock phrase literally: a thief deciding whether to take an object or leave it behind.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom presents an offer as fixed, so the hearer must simply accept or decline it.

clue.text: Brilliant essayist visiting hospital department

indicators.note: a visitor calls on a place, so the writer comes first and the department follows straight after

blocks.note: Charles Lamb, the English essayist who wrote as Elia
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A gifted writer of essays calling in at a hospital unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brilliant' looks like praise for the essayist but means shining. Charles Lamb wrote the Essays of Elia.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambent means softly glowing or flickering, and figuratively sparkling, as of light or wit.

clue.text: Halfway through, I'd stammer uncontrollably

indicators.note: uncontrollably suggests lack of order, so the letters break loose and regroup

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A nervous speaker admitting they would stammer partway through a talk.
explanation.definitionFit: In midstream means in the middle of an activity, an idiom for partway through.

clue.text: Really try in a series of IOM races

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the series of races that follows

blocks.note: to hear a case is to try it in court
A plus TT, the Tourist Trophy motorcycle races on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Urging someone to make a real effort in the Isle of Man motorcycle races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'try' looks like an attempt but is the judicial sense. HEAR sits inside A TT, between the two Ts.
explanation.definitionFit: At heart means fundamentally or in truth, matching really as an adverb of genuine nature.

clue.text: Came to be expelled

blocks.note: first meaning: proved to be
second meaning: thrown out of a place

explanation.surface: Someone who ended up being thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both resulted or proved to be, and evicted or ejected someone.

clue.text: Play trick on purpose

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the first piece follows the second in the across light

blocks.note: an end is an aim or purpose
a game is a scheme or trick, as in 'what's your game?'

explanation.surface: Pulling a prank deliberately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on purpose' reads as deliberately, but 'on' just places the trick after the purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: The endgame is the final stage of play in chess, so the answer names a phase of play.

clue.text: Fish — extremely exquisite head of panchax crushed by yobbo

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the next word, its outermost letters
head of picks out only the first letter of the following word
something crushed by another is squeezed inside it

blocks.note: the first and last letters of exquisite
a lout is a yobbo, a rough young man
first letter of panchax

explanation.surface: A delicate tropical fish crushed underfoot by a thug.
explanation.walkthrough: A panchax is a small aquarium fish, which helps hide the wordplay. P sits inside LOUT, after L. A yobbo is British slang for a hooligan.
explanation.definitionFit: The eelpout is an eel-like marine fish of northern waters, also called the viviparous blenny.

clue.text: Frankness, and in court! Not quite

indicators.note: not quite means falling just short, so the final letter is dropped
in puts the first word inside the shortened word that follows

blocks.note: taken as written
court with its last letter removed

explanation.surface: A witness praised for honesty, and in court too, though not entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation and 'Not quite' read as a comment on the witness, but they trim the word court.
explanation.definitionFit: Candour is the quality of being open and honest in speech, a synonym for frankness.

clue.text: Rhythm of exotic dance taped by church

indicators.note: exotic means strange and foreign, so the following word is rearranged
something taped by another is bound round by it, so it sits inside

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: The beat of a foreign dance recorded in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taped' suggests recording, but it means bound round.
explanation.definitionFit: Cadence is the rhythmic rise and fall of sound or movement, a synonym for rhythm.

clue.text: What bark beetles help to cause, causes the middle to rot

definitions.text: What bark beetles help to cause

indicators.note: something left to rot breaks down and falls apart, so the letters are reformed

blocks.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: Describing a tree disease spread by beetles that rots the heart of the trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is almost a description of the disease itself, which makes the anagram easy to miss.
explanation.definitionFit: Elm bark beetles carry the fungus responsible for this fatal tree blight, so they help spread it.

clue.text: Follow scholar, teaching

blocks.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
MA, a Master of Arts, is a scholar

explanation.surface: Advice to imitate a learned person's instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'teaching' looks like a verb but is a noun, a body of doctrine.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogma is a set of principles laid down by an authority, as in a church's teaching.

clue.text: Excuse used by Mexicali billionaire

indicators.note: used by suggests the answer is carried within the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the city name and the start of the next word

explanation.surface: A wealthy man from Mexicali giving an excuse.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed grid answer ALBII is a misprint. Mexicali is a Mexican border city.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of being elsewhere at the time of a crime, and loosely any excuse.

clue.text: Raw, inexperienced youth in new house on outskirts of Ripon

indicators.note: the outskirts of a town are its edges, so only the word's end letters are kept
on means set next to, so the house piece is followed by the edge letters

blocks.note: green means new or fresh, as of unripe wood or a novice
HO is the abbreviation for house
the first and last letters of Ripon

explanation.surface: A naive young man living in a newly built house on the edge of Ripon, a Yorkshire cathedral city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raw' looks like it supplies GREEN, but it belongs to the definition; GREEN comes from 'new', and 'in' links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A greenhorn is a novice lacking experience, so a raw, untried young person.

clue.text: Friend in Potsdam, Igor

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: the letters straddle the end of the city's name and the start of the man's name

explanation.surface: Introducing a friend called Igor who lives in Potsdam.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed grid answer AMBGO is a misprint; the hidden word spans Potsdam and Igor, ignoring the comma.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend and is widely used in English as an informal word for a pal.

clue.text: Top expert banking millions

indicators.note: banking means putting safely away inside, so the expert holds the next piece

blocks.note: an ace is a highly skilled person
M is the abbreviation for millions

explanation.surface: A leading financial expert who has stashed away millions.
explanation.walkthrough: M goes inside ACE, between C and E.
explanation.definitionFit: The acme is the highest point or peak of something, a synonym for the top.

clue.text: Holy man in street, Arnold perhaps

blocks.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
Benedict Arnold, the American general who defected to the British, is an example of someone with this first name

explanation.surface: A saintly figure spotted out on the street, possibly called Arnold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arnold perhaps' means a person named Benedict, as in the American traitor Benedict Arnold; 'in' just joins the two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Benedict founded Western monasticism, so he is a holy man, the ST standing for saint.
